Coverage CI (Codecov, first pass)

Source: .github/coverage.md

clade’s R package and Julia kernel both live in this repository (R/, tests/testthat/, inst/julia/). Coverage is collected from the suites GitHub Actions already runs, then uploaded once per language flag. pigauto, GLLVModels, and other repositories are out of scope.

What is measured

Flag Existing suite Honest meaning
r .github/workflows/tests.yaml: devtools::test() with CLADE_SKIP_JULIA_TESTS=true covr instruments the installed package, then testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat", package = "clade", load_package = "installed") from the checkout (same files, namespace and skip as tests.yaml; any failure or error fails the job). Default package_coverage() / test_check() runs from the install, where repo-root scanners resolve to the installed dir with no vignettes/*.Rmd and fail NULL vs character(0) (2 failures). Bare test_dir() without package= fails test-stream-submit.R (local_mocked_bindings needs a package). Per-test results are in artifact coverage-r (coverage-r-results.csv). Do not use devtools::test() inside covr (load_all() drops instrumentation). Julia-dependent R tests skip, so kernel-driven R paths are uncovered here on purpose.
julia .github/workflows/julia-tests.yaml: julia --project=inst/julia inst/julia/test/runtests.jl line coverage of inst/julia/src from that unit suite (--code-coverage=user added only for instrumentation).

R-CMD-check.yaml uses --no-tests and does not produce coverage. fidelity-matrix.yaml is a manual reproduction harness, not the existing PR suite.

The tests and julia-tests jobs remain the assertion gates. This workflow does not change their skip rules, expectations, or timeouts.

Who uploads

Only .github/workflows/coverage.yaml. Do not add:

  • covr::codecov()
  • Coverage.jl Codecov.submit / Codecov.submit_local
  • a second GitHub workflow that posts the same files
  • token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} or token: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}

Each job uploads one file with disable_search: true (coverage-r.xml or lcov.info) so the two flags cannot pick up each other’s reports.

OIDC, least privilege

Authentication is GitHub Actions OIDC (codecov-action use_oidc: true). There is no Codecov upload token in this repository.

Permissions are job-scoped, not workflow-wide write:

permissions:
  contents: read   # checkout
  id-token: write  # request an OIDC JWT for Codecov; not repo write

GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} on the R job is only for r-lib package install. It must never be passed to codecov-action as token.

Owner action after a real uploader failure (codecov-action log showing OIDC rejected or upload HTTP error): install/enable the Codecov GitHub App with OIDC for itchyshin/clade, or add a dedicated Codecov upload token secret. A Codecov dashboard “Configure” screen or an API response of unknown/empty is not that proof. Do not reuse GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN as the Codecov token.

Fork PRs cannot mint OIDC tokens; same-repo branches can.

Checkout identity

pull_request jobs use actions/checkout@v4 with no ref: override, so they test the synthetic merge commit (github.sha), not the exact PR head, unless the job log prints tested_equals_exact_head=true. Exact head and base SHAs are printed in “Record coverage checkout identity”. push to main tests that ref exactly.

Stages of evidence

Keep these separate. Passing one is not passing the next.

  1. Config — this document, coverage.yaml, .github/codecov.yml.
  2. Coverage execution / percent — job logs and the coverage-r / coverage-julia artifacts (percent_coverage=…).
  3. Upload reception — codecov-action log (OIDC, commit, flag, HTTP).
  4. Processed report — Codecov UI for this SHA/flags.
  5. Default-main baseline — authorized owner merge to main plus a successful coverage workflow on main. Do not merge from the coverage agent. Do not add README badges before stage 5.

Status checks in .github/codecov.yml are informational so a missing baseline cannot look like a coverage-gate failure.

Local runtimes

This workflow needs R (covr) and Julia 1.10. If those are missing on a given machine, say so and rely on CI for execution-stage numbers.
